questions.q: How does the TOGAF Standard treat the enterprise when developing an architecture?
o: As a single legal entity only
As a system, for which one or several EAs may be developed
As a collection of unrelated projects
questions.e: TOGAF treats the enterprise as a system; you may develop one EA for the whole corporation or several independent EAs for divisions, depending on goals and resources.

questions.q: Which characteristic makes TOGAF suitable as an enterprise architecture framework?
o: It is a rigid method that cannot be changed
It is generic and best-practice, intended to be tailored to the enterprise
It only works for government agencies
It prescribes a single mandatory toolset
questions.e: TOGAF is a generic, community-developed best-practice framework designed to be tailored and used standalone or integrated with frameworks like ITIL, COBIT, and PRINCE2.

questions.q: Which architecture domain describes business strategy, governance, organization, and key business processes?
questions.e: The Business Architecture describes business strategy, governance, organization, and key business processes, including capabilities and value streams.

questions.q: What does the Enterprise Continuum primarily provide?
o: A categorization for structuring and classifying reusable architecture and solution assets
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum is a categorization for structuring and classifying reusable assets held in the enterprise repositories, from generic to specific.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository holds Solution Building Blocks, whether planned or deployed?
questions.e: The Solutions Landscape holds the Solution Building Blocks that support the Architecture Landscape, planned or deployed.

questions.q: According to the notes, what is the correct wording for what the 'new' row of a gap analysis identifies?
o: Items to be developed or produced
Items to be developed or procured
questions.e: The 'new' row lists what to build or buy: developed or procured. The notes flag that 'developed or produced' is an error; correct is developed or procured.

questions.q: Where does Requirements Management sit relative to the eight lettered phases?
o: At the centre of the ADM cycle
Between Phases D and E only
questions.e: Requirements Management sits at the centre of the ADM cycle and operates continuously across the phases.

questions.q: Which statement about 'approved' deliverables is the common exam trap answer to avoid?
o: Approved means reviewed and signed off
Approved means finalized and unable to change
Approved deliverables may still evolve via change control
questions.e: The trap is equating approved with finalized. Approved means reviewed and signed off; approved deliverables may still evolve via change control.

questions.q: Which of the following best characterizes the ADM?
o: An iterative method applied over the whole process, between phases, and within phases
A fixed sequence that cannot be tailored
questions.e: The ADM is iterative over the whole process, between phases, and within phases; it is not a waterfall and is tailored under governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the three purposes of the Preliminary Phase?
o: Finalize the Implementation and Migration Plan
Approve the Statement of Architecture Work
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase has three purposes: create the architecture capability, tailor the framework, and define architecture principles.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of Phase A, Architecture Vision?
o: Define scope, identify stakeholders, and create the Architecture Vision
questions.e: Phase A defines scope, identifies stakeholders, creates the Architecture Vision, and obtains approval to proceed.

questions.q: Which artifact is typically the starting point for the Application Architecture in Phase C?
questions.e: The Application Portfolio Catalog, a list of logical and physical application components, is usually the starting point for the Application Architecture.

questions.q: Which deliverable is first produced in Phase E and consolidates work packages and Transition Architectures?
questions.e: The Architecture Roadmap is first produced in Phase E, consolidating work packages and Transition Architectures on a timeline; it is adjusted in Phase F.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Phase F, Migration Planning?
o: To identify delivery vehicles for the first time
To finalize the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and transition governance to realizing the EA
questions.e: Phase F finalizes the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and transitions governance from developing to realizing the EA.

questions.q: Which deliverable is the simplest means to ensure implementation conforms to the target architecture in Phase G?
questions.e: The Architecture Contract, a joint agreement between development partners and sponsors realized through governance, is one of the simplest means to ensure conformance to the target.

questions.q: From which phases does a Change Request typically originate before it is assessed in Phase H?
questions.e: Change Requests originate in Phase F (lessons learned) and Phase G (implementation deviations or scope extensions), and are assessed in Phase H.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Requirements Management phase?
o: To manage architecture requirements and maintain the complete set as a single point of truth with traceability
questions.e: Requirements Management documents, evaluates, and distributes requirements, manages their change, provides traceability, and maintains the complete set as a single point of truth.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated purpose of architecture principles?
o: To act as the contract between sponsor and architect
To enable decision-making by setting precedence during trade-off discussions
To assess organizational readiness for change
questions.e: Principles enable decision-making by setting precedence during trade-offs, align the enterprise, support governance, and reflect values and culture.

questions.q: Where are architecture principles kept, and what do they trace back to?
o: In the Solutions Landscape, tracing to SBBs
In a Principles Catalog, tracing back to business objectives and drivers
In the Change Log, tracing to dispensations
In the Communications Plan, tracing to stakeholders
questions.e: Architecture principles are kept in a Principles Catalog and trace back to business objectives and drivers; they are enduring and seldom amended.

questions.q: Which criterion means a principle allows a balanced, flexible interpretation without contradictions?
questions.e: Consistent means the principle allows balanced, flexible interpretation without contradictions. Complete covers every situation; Stable is enduring yet accommodates change.

questions.q: A business scenario is distinct from which of the following?
o: A technique for identifying and understanding business needs
A use case model focused on human-to-computer detail
A means of deriving architecture requirements
A deliverable used in Phases A and B
questions.e: A business scenario identifies business needs and derives requirements; it is distinct from a use case model (human-to-computer detail), a business case, or a sales technique.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognized form of interoperability?
questions.e: The three forms are operational/business, information, and technical interoperability; interoperability is the ability to share information as well as services.

questions.q: Which ADM phase is described as the location for initial identification of business transformation risks and their mitigation activities?
questions.e: Initial identification of business transformation risks and their mitigations is a Phase A step. Risk monitoring and governance (using worksheets) is addressed in Phase G. Phase E addresses risk when evaluating opportunities and solutions.

questions.q: Before starting an iteration, which factors must the architect decide as part of the scope?
o: Breadth, depth, time period, and which architectural assets to reuse
questions.e: Before each iteration the architect decides breadth, depth, time period, and which architectural assets to reuse, based on available resources and expected value.

questions.q: The three levels of the Architecture Landscape are distinguished chiefly by which attributes?
questions.e: Strategic, Segment, and Capability levels are distinguished by breadth of scope, level of detail, and time horizon.

questions.q: Which statement about the architecture partitioning model is correct?
o: TOGAF prescribes one definitive partitioning model for all enterprises
There is no single definitive model; it should reflect the enterprise's operating model
Partitioning applies only to the Technology Architecture
Each partition must be owned by several teams
questions.e: There is no single definitive partitioning model; each enterprise adopts one reflecting its operating model, and each partition has one owning team.

questions.q: Which scope dimension articulates the planning horizon that must be doable with available resources?
questions.e: Time Period articulates the planning horizon for the vision and must be achievable with available resources. The four dimensions are Breadth, Depth, Time Period, and Architecture Domain.

questions.q: How is Architecture Governance related to corporate governance?
o: It is entirely separate from corporate governance
It is part of corporate governance and directs and controls the EA enterprise-wide
It applies only within a single project
questions.e: Architecture Governance is part of corporate governance; it directs and controls the EA at an enterprise-wide level within a hierarchy of governance structures.

questions.q: Which best describes the composition of an Architecture Board?
o: A cross-organizational body of key architecture stakeholders, usually executives
questions.e: The Architecture Board is a cross-organizational body of key architecture stakeholders, usually executives, responsible for review and maintenance of the EA.

questions.q: Why should Architecture Contracts establish joint agreements between all parties involved in delivery?
o: Because principles no longer apply during delivery
Because more delivery is done by integrators and providers, so joint accountability is needed
Because the sponsor is the only relevant party
Because contracts are created in the Preliminary Phase
questions.e: Because more delivery is done by integrators and providers, Architecture Contracts establish joint agreements ensuring accountability, monitoring, and adherence to principles and standards.

questions.q: In an Architecture Compliance Review, what dual role does the architect play?
questions.e: The architect acts as auditor and advisor: assessing compliance at milestones and recommending enforcement, dispensation, or a change to the target. Stakeholders approve.

questions.q: Which pairing correctly maps the memory hook 'the lens' and 'what you see through it'?
o: View = the lens; Viewpoint = what you see
Viewpoint = the lens; View = what you see
Neither is a lens; they are diagrams
questions.e: Viewpoint is the generic, reusable lens; the view is the specific instance you see through it, built for actual stakeholders and their concerns.

questions.q: How does the TOGAF Standard define a 'concern'?
o: An interest in a system relevant to one or more stakeholders
questions.e: A concern is an interest in a system relevant to one or more stakeholders, covering matters such as performance, reliability, security, and evolvability; concerns lead to requirements.

questions.q: In which phases are ABBs typically identified and then refined into SBBs?
o: ABBs identified in Phases A-D; refined into SBBs in Phase E
ABBs identified in Phase E; refined into SBBs in Phase A
Both identified only in Phase H
Both identified in the Preliminary Phase
questions.e: ABBs are identified in Phases A-D; selected ABBs are refined into SBBs in Phase E (purchase or develop).

questions.q: Which deliverable documents an assessment of the organization's capabilities and is first produced early in Phase A?
questions.e: The Capability Assessment evaluates capabilities (business, IT, architecture maturity, business transformation readiness) as a first step of Phase A and feeds phases B-G.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the ADD from the Architecture Vision?
o: The ADD is high-level and aspirational; the Vision is the artifact container
The ADD is the qualitative container for core artifacts; the Vision is the high-level aspirational summary
The Vision is quantitative; the ADD is a communication timetable
questions.e: The ADD is the qualitative container for core artifacts; the Architecture Vision is the high-level aspirational summary and early view of the full Architecture Definition.

questions.q: Which deliverable finalized in Phase F provides the schedule of projects showing 'how' the transformation is delivered?
questions.e: The Implementation and Migration Plan is the schedule of projects showing 'how' the transformation is delivered; it is first produced in Phase E and finalized in Phase F. The Roadmap shows 'what'.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Compliance Assessment deliverable?
o: To trigger a new architecture cycle
To ensure the realized design and implementation align with the strategic and architectural objectives and the vision
To communicate to stakeholders on a timetable
To define the scope and approach of the cycle
questions.e: The Architecture Compliance Assessment ensures the realized design and implementation align with the strategic and architectural objectives and the vision; used in Phase G and H.

questions.q: The top-level structure of the Content Framework is organized in which way?
o: It mirrors the phases of the ADM
questions.e: The Content Framework's top-level structure mirrors the ADM phases, acting as a companion to the ADM and defining which work products to develop.

questions.q: Which of the four 'purpose' capabilities supports change and synergies across programs and portfolios with a 3-10 year horizon?
questions.e: The Support Strategy capability addresses change, synergies, and governance across programs and portfolios with low detail and a 3-10 year horizon. Support Project and Solution Delivery are narrow and short-term.
